cards.text: Job just said, "But I know that my Redeemer lives…" (Job 19:25). Now Zophar the Naamathite, one of the three friends who came to comfort Job (Job 2:11), replies. And friend, he is NOT easing into it.
Zophar opens by saying something inside him won't let him stay quiet. Like when a message comes in and you're typing back before you even finish reading it.

cards.question: Zophar says something inside him compels him to answer Job. What is it?
True or false: Zophar says he has heard a rebuke that insults him.

cards.text: Then Zophar asks Job, "Do you not know…" He's about to bring up something he says has been true for a long, LONG time.

cards.question: Zophar says this truth about the wicked is old. How far back does he say it goes?

answers.text: Since man was placed on the earth

cards.question: Zophar's whole speech is about the wicked. He says that all that time, the triumph of the wicked has been ___.

cards.text: Then Zophar says, though the wicked man's arrogance reaches the heavens and his head touches the clouds... Friend, I stretch ALL the way up on my gold base and my head touches the second oven rack.

cards.question: Zophar says that even with his head up in the clouds, the wicked man will ___ forever.

cards.text: And Zophar picks a blunt picture for it: the wicked man will perish forever, "like his own dung…"

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the people who once saw the wicked man will ask, ‘Where is he?’

cards.text: Zophar says the wicked man will fly away like a dream, chased away like a vision in the night. Like the dream you SWEAR you'll remember, and by the second snooze it's GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the eye that saw the wicked man will see him again someday.

cards.text: Zophar says even the wicked man's place won't behold him anymore. Oh, I know that one, friend: the day a shiny new stamper took MY spot on the counter, I ended up in the back of the junk drawer.

cards.question: Zophar says the wicked man's own hands must give his wealth back. So what does he say the man's sons will do?

answers.text: Seek the favor of the poor

cards.question: Zophar talks about the youthful vigor that fills the wicked man's bones. Where does he say it ends up?

answers.text: Lying with him in the dust

cards.text: Now Zophar switches to a picture of eating. Though evil is sweet in the wicked man's mouth and he hides it under his tongue, though he can't bear to let it go, like that last bite of cookie you keep in your cheek so nobody asks you to share…

cards.question: Zophar says the wicked man keeps that sweet evil in his mouth. What happens to his food once it's in his stomach?

answers.text: His food sours into cobra venom
His food makes him strong again
His food stays sweet inside him

cards.question: Zophar keeps going with the eating picture. He says the wicked man swallows ___ but vomits it out, and God will force it from his stomach.

cards.text: Then Zophar says the wicked man will suck the poison of cobras, and the fangs of a viper will kill him.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man will enjoy the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

cards.text: Zophar says the wicked man must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it, and he can't enjoy the profits of his trading. Like payday hitting and the bills taking it ALL before you even see it.

cards.question: Now Zophar says why the wicked man loses everything he worked for. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He oppressed and forsook the poor
He gave his wealth to strangers

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man seized houses he did not build.
Zophar keeps coming back to food and swallowing. What does he say about the wicked man's appetite?

cards.text: And Zophar says that's why the wicked man can't escape with his treasure.
Then Zophar says nothing is left for him to consume, so his prosperity won't last. Like me "tasting" the chocolate chips until there are none left for the batch.

cards.question: True or false: Zophar says the wicked man will be at peace as long as he has plenty.
True or false: Zophar says that when the wicked man has filled his stomach, God will rain down His fury on him as he eats.
Zophar says the wicked man flees from an iron weapon. What does Zophar say happens to him next?

cards.text: Zophar says the arrow is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver, and terrors come over him. This part of Zophar's speech is heavy, friend.

cards.question: Zophar says total darkness is reserved for the wicked man's treasures, and a fire nobody fanned will consume him. What else does he say that fire devours?

answers.text: What is left in his tent

cards.question: Zophar turns to the sky above the wicked man. He says the heavens will ___ his iniquity.

cards.text: Zophar says the earth will rise up against him too, and the possessions of his house will flow away on the day of God's wrath. Sky on one side, ground on the other, and that man has NOWHERE left to stand.

cards.question: Zophar wraps up his whole speech in one line. What does he call everything he just described?

answers.text: The wicked man's portion from God

cards.text: That's Zophar's whole speech, friend. And trust me, this conversation is FAR from over.
